references.text: The command to keep the Sabbath holy, which is part of the Ten Commandments given to Moses on Sinai.
The Sabbath as a sign between God and the children of Israel, with the command to keep it holy.
Earlier in the same chapter, the command to keep the Sabbaths is repeated, along with reverence for parents.
A nearly identical verse that repeats the command to keep the Sabbaths and to have reverence for the sanctuary.
God's sanctuary (mishkan) as the place where the Lord's glory dwells, and which requires reverence.
Repetition of the Sabbath command in the Ten Commandments in Deuteronomy.
A prophetic blessing upon those who keep the Sabbath and do not profane it.
The Sabbaths given as a sign between the Lord and his people so that they may know that he is the Lord.
An accusation against those who profane the Sabbaths and despise God's holy things.
A call to serve God with reverence, for our God is a consuming fire.
